newsitem.title: KENYA: Trade overshadowed by tension at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Trade overshadowed by tension at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Business was slow at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE), overshadowed by tension in the city's commercial centre ahead of the presentation of the state budget.
Brokers said activity was down with many of them ending trading a quarter-hour before the official market close.

"Many brokers came to the floor with hands folded," a senior broker said, adding that fears that a proposed pro-democracy march in defiance of a government ban had affected the volume of trading in the market.
The NSE 20-share index was down 6.29 points to close at 3468.10. Turnover was posted at 12.1 million shillings traded on 309,610 compared to 14.9 million shillings on 368,311 shares.
Market players are hoping that the government will increase the level of foreign investor participation in listed companies in this afternoon's budget speech.
Currently foreign investors are allowed a maximum of 40 percent ownership in a local firm as a company and five percent as individual investors.
"We have a lot of buy orders waiting. Many of our foreign clients have asked us to wait until after the budget is read," a broker from a leading trading house said.
Kenya Commercial Bank traded at 105 unchanged while Barclays Bank traded at 113 unchanged.
Brooke Bond was unchanged at 125 while Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 9.05 unchanged.
Uchumi Supermarket was unchanged at 40 while Kenya Airways edged to 8.35 from 8.10.
Firestone East Africa was unchanged at 28.25 while Kenya Power & Lighting closed at 176 unchanged.
